query_parsed: Give me a long passage from "A Game of Thrones" by George R.R. Martin.
ai_generated_output_text:
Here is a pivotal and atmospheric passage from the first book of the series, A Game of Thrones. This scene takes place shortly after Lord Eddard Stark has executed a deserter of the Night’s Watch, as he and his sons come across a discovery that will change the fate of House Stark forever.The Discovery of the Direwolves"The snows had buried the road, but the track was still plain to see. They rode in single file, the Northmen and the boys, through the ancient, silent woods.
It was Jon who found them. He had been riding ahead, his eyes searching the shadows for the elk they had been tracking since dawn. Instead, he found something else. He was off his horse and kneeling in the snow by the time the others reached him.
'Is it a wolf?' Robb asked, swinging down from his saddle.
'A direwolf,' Jon said. He was holding a bundle of fur and flesh, and the pup was making a small, whimpering sound.
Bran dismounted and ran to join them. He had never seen a direwolf, but he had heard the stories. They were larger than any hound, as big as ponies, with teeth like daggers. This one was tiny, its eyes still closed, but even so, it looked fierce.
'There are more,' Jon said. He pointed to the dead mother.
She was a massive beast, her fur matted with dried blood and frozen slush. A jagged piece of antler was buried deep in her throat, the broken tine of a great elk. She had died in the act of killing, it seemed.
'The pups,' Ned said, his voice heavy. He looked down at the dead mother and then at the five small, squirming shapes that were huddled against her cold belly. 'They won’t survive without their mother.'
'We should kill them,' Theon Greyjoy said, drawing his sword. 'It’s a mercy.'
'No!' Bran cried. He looked at his father, his eyes pleading. 'Please, Father.'
Ned Stark looked at his sons. He saw the way Bran was looking at the pups, and he saw the way Robb was holding one of them. He looked at Jon, who was standing a little apart, as he always did.
'Lord Stark,' Jon said, his voice quiet but firm. 'There are five pups. One for each of your legal children. Three sons, two daughters. The direwolf is the sigil of House Stark. They were meant to have them.'
Bran saw his father’s face change. He saw the way his eyes softened, just for a moment.
'You have no pup for yourself, Jon,' Ned said.
'I am no Stark,' Jon said.
It was then that they heard it. A small, faint sound, like the scratching of a mouse. Jon turned and walked a few paces away, to where a white pup was crawling through the snow. Its fur was as white as the snow itself, and its eyes, when it finally opened them, were a deep, burning red.
'An albino,' Theon said, with a short, sharp laugh. 'This one will die even faster than the others.'
'I think not,' Jon said, picking up the white pup. 'This one belongs to me.'"Context and SignificanceThis moment is heavy with the foreshadowing that George R.R. Martin is famous for. A few key things to notice:The Omen: The mother direwolf (the sigil of House Stark) was killed by an elk’s antler (the stag is the sigil of House Baratheon). This subtly hints at the lethal entanglement between the Starks and the Crown.The Numbers: There are five "trueborn" pups for the five Stark children, but Jon finds the sixth—an outsider, just like himself.Ghost: The discovery of the albino pup, who opened his eyes before the others and wandered off alone, perfectly mirrors Jon Snow’s journey as the "White Wolf" of the North.</ul
